transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-06-17
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (AtlasRetail), Jenna Li (AtlasRetail SRE), Marcus Rowe (ML Eng), Priya Kaur (AtlasRetail Sec)

Summary (auto): quick sync on onboarding, access blockers, results from last week's smoke tests; action items assigned.

[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, uh thanks for joining. Quick roll call, we got Samir, Jenna, Marcus, Priya?
[00:07] Samir Patel: Here, sorry I'm a bit late, had a calendar clash, but all good now.
[00:10] Marco Diaz: Cool. Quick agenda: access status, smoke test metrics, security ask, then next steps.
[00:16] Jenna Li: Access: created the staging subnet, we've got a couple of firewall rules to tweak - egress to Redwood service IPs needs to be opened, and we need the peering route.
[00:25] Lena Park: OK that matches our note. Samir, can you confirm which team will open the ports?
[00:29] Samir Patel: Jenna's team will do it, but I need the exact CIDR and port range from Redwood. We thought Redwood would accept TLS on 443 only but your doc mentioned a range for health checks?
[00:39] Marco Diaz: Right, health checks come from ephemeral workers so we recommend 443 and an outbound ephemeral range 30000-32767 for internal health and metrics. We'll also accept traffic over 443.
[00:49] Jenna Li: Got it, we'll open 443 and the ephemeral range. I'll put the exact rule in the ticket after this call.
[00:54] Marcus Rowe: Quick question on the smoke tests you ran last week — throughput looked good but latency had a few spikes. Are those expected with small batch sizes?
[01:03] Marco Diaz: Yeah, mm-hmm, so the initial run was on default batching which is conservative. For your workload we suggested the continuous batching profile, that reduces per-token cost but can add 20-30ms median depending on concurrency. The spikes were tied to cold KV cache misses.
[01:19] Marcus Rowe: Cold KV cache misses — can you explain that again, I think the transcript had kv-cache as kv-cash earlier, so just making sure we mean the key-value KV cache for model context?
[01:27] Marco Diaz: Sorry, kv-cache, yes. It's the prefix cache — when a customer sends repeated prompts, the cache prevents recomputation of early tokens. On first run we saw misses which cause short spikes. If you warm the cache or use the longer-lived cache TTL it'll smooth out.
[01:40] Priya Kaur: On security, we need to confirm KMS usage and key residency. Are you using Redwood-managed keys by default? We need customer-managed KMS and audit logs for the pilot to be compliant with our internal policy.
[01:52] Lena Park: Good question. For the hosted POC we're offering customer-managed keys (CMK) for the staging environment. We'll share the steps; Marco can attach the KMS integration doc. Audit logs — yes, we can enable syslogs to your Splunk/Datadog endpoint, and we provide request-level logging for the pilot.
[02:07] Marco Diaz: I'll add the KMS and audit log walkthrough to the pack. Note: for Private/VPC installs there's an optional HSM/KMS toggle, but for hosted we do bring-your-own KMS via IAM roles.
[02:19] Samir Patel: That works. One caveat — we're under a contract with our procurement to limit external managed keys to specific vendors. I'll loop in procurement if needed.
[02:26] Lena Park: Understood. We'll include both patterns in the doc so you can present to procurement.
[02:30] Jenna Li: Another infra question — will we need to open inbound ports to a Redwood endpoint, or is this outbound-only from our VPC?
[02:36] Marco Diaz: It's outbound-only. You call the Redwood API over TLS to the dedicated endpoint; peering is optional for lower latency. If you want the dedicated throughput we can set up Dedicated pool and peer that into your VPC, which would require a route, not inbound firewall openings.
[02:49] Marcus Rowe: On performance numbers, can you re-share the test config? Last run said 50 concurrent sessions, 256 token windows, and quantized model variant?
[02:58] Marco Diaz: Yes: 50 concurrency, 256 context, model q4_k_m variant (we used a quantized open model for cost). That tradeoff reduced tokens costs about 40% but added ~10% latency at tail. We'll log both token cost and P95 latency.
[03:15] Samir Patel: The cost numbers look promising but procurement will want a per-inference cost estimate at our expected peak. Can you provide the spreadsheet you used?
[03:22] Lena Park: We'll share the benchmark spreadsheet. Marco can run another small-batch test matching your expected peak and dump the numbers.
[03:28] Marco Diaz: Yep, I'll run a run matching the pattern you shared — 200 QPS burst with 50 concurrency sustained for 10 minutes — and include token cost, median and P95 latencies.
[03:36] Jenna Li: Timeline?
[03:38] Marco Diaz: I can run it tomorrow and post results by 6/20.
[03:41] Priya Kaur: For compliance review, do you have a SOC2 cert scanned and a contact for security questionnaire?
[03:47] Lena Park: Yes, SOC2 Type II is available. I'll attach the cert and the security questionnaire contact — that's part of the security pack.
[03:54] Samir Patel: Great. Also, question about data retention: will logs for the pilot be retained longer than 30 days by default? We want 90 days for troubleshooting.
[04:02] Marco Diaz: Default retention is 30 for the hosted tier but we can configure a 90-day window for the pilot as an add-on. We'll note cost implications.
[04:11] Marcus Rowe: For the model variants — if we need to fall back to a cheaper variant during high load, does Redwood do automatic fallback?
[04:18] Marco Diaz: There's a routing policy you can set. For the POC we can configure automatic fallback to a cheaper quantized model when latency or capacity thresholds hit. That keeps availability up but may affect output quality.
[04:28] Marcus Rowe: Ok good to know. One last technical: will you need any agents installed in our VPC, or is everything remote?
[04:34] Marco Diaz: No agent required for hosted. For Private installation we do have an optional connector for metrics and health checks, but it's not needed for the hosted pilot.
[04:42] Lena Park: Alright let's recap actions — Lena to send SOC2 + infra diagram; Marco to run the 200 QPS bench and share spreadsheet; Samir/Jenna to provide subnet CIDR and open ports; Jenna to create service account and share keys. Next sync next week.
[04:57] Samir Patel: Sounds good. One minor note: we might want a short deep-dive on the KV cache behaviour with Marcus, can we schedule 30 minutes?
[05:05] Marco Diaz: Absolutely — I'll set up a technical deep dive for KV cache and batching behavior for the week after next.
[05:11] Priya Kaur: I'll review the security pack when you send it. Thanks everyone.
[05:15] Lena Park: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and results.
[05:18] Jenna Li: Bye.

Notes:
- Slight transcription errors expected (product names: Redwood Dedicated sometimes transcribed as 'Readwood dedicated').
- References to quantization variants (q4_k_m), KV cache, peering, KMS, SOC2, and routing/fallback policies present.
- Links referenced during call: "Security pack (link)"; "Benchmark spreadsheet (link)" — not included in transcript per policy.

End of transcript.
